chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Abul Abbas al-Siraj narrated to us, saying: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Rashdin ibn Sa'd al-Misri, Abul Hajjaj, narrated to us, saying: Sharahil ibn Yazid narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
When a man's heart is pure, his body is pure; and when the heart is diseased, the body becomes diseased.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the heart and the body in Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal underscores the Shia concept of the holistic unity of the human being, where the heart (qalb) serves as the spiritual center governing physical well-being. It reflects the prophetic tradition that moral integrity (akhlaq) directly influences physiological health, a theme often explored in Shia tafsir and hadith sciences regarding the 'organ' of the body.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-110 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Abul Abbas al-Suraj quoted on the authority of Abul Abbas al-Siraj quoted on the authority of Qutaybat, on the authority of Roshdin ibn Sa’ed al-Mesri Abul Haj’jaj , on the authority of Sharahil ibn Yazid , on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar and AbiHurayrih that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“When a man’s heart is healthy, then his body is healthy. If the heart is diseased, then the body will become diseased.”
